features.name: New-game configuration and launch
steps: Tap NEW GAME on the home page
Choose the board size 4×4 / 5×5 / 6×6 in the new-game panel
Choose the difficulty Easy / Medium / Hard
features.expected: It must handle 3 board sizes × 3 difficulties in combination; the selected item should be clearly highlighted; after entering the game the digit button range must match N, e.g. 4×4 shows only 1–4 and 6×6 shows 1–6

features.name: Basic Futoshiki number input
steps: Tap the digits at the bottom
The number is written into that cell
Then select another cell and continue entering
features.expected: The initially given numbers cannot be modified; user-entered numbers and preset numbers should have an observable state difference; the selected cell and input feedback must be correct; the number of digit keys changes dynamically with the board size

features.name: Row/column uniqueness rules
steps: Try entering an already-existing number in the same row or column
Change it to a legal number
features.expected: Every row and every column must ultimately contain each of 1..N exactly once; duplicate numbers must be detected rather than only comparing the whole-board answer at final submission; error cells should give feedback such as turning red according to the target UI

features.name: Inequality constraint rules
steps: Find two adjacent cells with >, <, or up/down inequality hints
Enter a set of numbers that satisfies the relationships
Then try entering a number that violates the relationship
features.expected: The direction interpretation must be fully correct. The comparison operators indicate the size relationship between adjacent cells; not only horizontal but also vertical constraints must be correct; it must not implement only a Latin square while ignoring the inequalities

features.name: Joint validation of the full rule set
steps: Fill continuously combining row uniqueness, column uniqueness, and all inequalities
features.expected: This is the core reproduction task. A complete solution must satisfy all of: (1) one number per cell; (2) no repetition of 1..N in each row; (3) no repetition of 1..N in each column; (4) all inequalities hold; failing any one condition must not be judged as complete

features.name: Wrong input and the remaining mistake count
steps: Observe the error cells and the mistakes remaining at the top
features.expected: The screenshot already shows the error cell turning red and "4 mistakes remaining". The remaining mistake count must be maintained correctly; legal input must not deduct a mistake; the error state, number state, and remaining count must stay in sync; the behavior after the count runs out must match the original app

features.name: Easy / Medium / Hard difficulty differences
steps: Create Easy, Medium, and Hard separately on the same board size
Compare the initial given numbers, inequality layout, and solving complexity
features.expected: Difficulty must not be just a text label; different difficulties need to produce actually different puzzle constraint/clue structures. The three difficulty levels all belong to the same generation and solving system

features.name: Adaptive 4×4 / 5×5 / 6×6 boards
steps: Verify the row/column rules and inequalities
Complete games of at least different sizes among them
features.expected: All core algorithms must be parameterized to N×N: board layout, number range, constraint checks, solving, and completion detection must not be hard-coded to 4×4; this is the key task that distinguishes a "UI imitation" from a genuine logic reproduction

features.name: Dynamic puzzle generation with a unique solution
steps: Start several games in a row with the same "size + difficulty"
features.expected: The target app explicitly includes a puzzle generator with a unique-solution guarantee. F-Droid A new game must not always return a fixed template; the generated prefilled numbers and inequalities must be self-consistent and a unique complete solution must exist. This is one of the most important pieces of back-end logic

features.name: Game timing, pause, and resume
steps: Wait for the timing to increase
Wait for a period of time
features.expected: The timer at the top-right should run with the game; after Pause the board cannot continue to be operated normally and the timing behavior must match the target; after Resume the same board and existing input are restored; the ninja/dragon animated scene at the top should also match the game state

features.name: Reset the current game
steps: Fill several numbers on the board and produce several intermediate states
features.expected: Reset should clear this game's player input and restore the initial puzzle; the preset numbers and inequalities must be preserved; how in-game states such as the timer and mistake count are restored must match the original app, and a different puzzle must not be generated in place of a Reset

features.name: Successful completion and the victory page
steps: Correctly fill the last empty cell
Check the board size, difficulty, and SOLVED IN time
features.expected: Completion should be detected automatically after the last legal input; the victory page must show the corresponding Grid 4×4/5×5/6×6, Mode EASY/MEDIUM/HARD, and the real completion time; after a new game the previous game's state must not pollute the next one

features.name: Help / game-rules tutorial
steps: Enter HELP from the home page
Start the game and complete several inputs following the tutorial
features.expected: The tutorial page should explain the row/column uniqueness and inequality core rules; the page supports scrolling; BACK returns to the home page with normal navigation and no side effects on the game state

features.name: Theme system and visual-state preservation
steps: Enter THEMES from the home page
Switch between different themes (the screenshots include Sand, Fire, Water, Earth, etc.)
Return to the home page and enter the game
features.expected: The current version is confirmed to have 4 color themes and several theme modes. Fossdroid themes need to affect visuals such as button accent colors; the combined states of MONO/TINTED and AUTO/DAY/NIGHT must be saved correctly; switching themes must not change the puzzle business data
